title: Skapa as Upstream source in Azure Artifacts
content:
Introduction

Skapa is a design system that as a part includes components c.f. Kompis. The Skapa registry is public and hosted using A lightweight Node.js private proxy registry | Verdaccio

The logical way to consume Skapa packages would be to follow the pattern for package sharing within IPEX. This would imply to set Skapa as an Upstream source to the product feed in Azure Artifacts, configuring it as a custom public source. This does not work as expected and you get HTTP status code 502 - Bad Gateway.

Workaround

Details for this is described below for the interested but the current workaround is to include Skapa (outside Azure Artifacts) as described at NPM - INGKA (cdtapps.com) i.e. have @ingka:registry https://npm.m2.blue.cdtapps.com in npmrc file for application.

Investigation

During the investigation there has been several meetings with Microsoft support engineer and as well with Skapa team including PO robin.whittleton@ingka.ikea.com. The support case id is 2111020050002107 opened for Azure Subscription cbf-devops-prd.

Connecting from a local development machine installing Skapa packages including public dependencies form http://npmjs.org works.

If Skapa is configured as a public upstream source and Skapa packages is requested a HTTP 502 error is received. The reason for this is described in answer from Azure Artifacts product team.

“

  1. <NPMjs upstream is first one so why it is going to custom upstream . As for as i know , it will goes in order . Please correct me if i am wrong> Answer- It doesn't go in order, the feed makes calls to all of the up streams to find all versions. The order is used to determine where to get the package from once the server has all responses. In other words, the downstream feed asks all upstream feeds "Hey, do you have this?" and then gives preference on where to download the package based on the order and the version that you want.

    1. In this case, if you are trying to download package foo, and foo exists ONLY in npmjs then you get a 502 because:

      1. Feed asks all upstreams for the package metadata (aka, what versions do they have?)

        Custom public upstream returns a 401 because the package doesn't exist

        Server says "well that's not a valid response from the upstream"

        Server return 502

“

Skapa is looking into moving from Verdaccio so adding Skapa as an upstream source might be feasible in the future.
